name: Sermorelin

lead: Sermorelin is a synthetic fragment of growth hormone releasing hormone, made of its first 29 amino acids. People use it hoping to raise growth hormone for leanness, sleep, recovery and anti-ageing, and some teenagers hope for added height.

It acts on GHRH receptors in the pituitary to prompt natural pulsatile GH release, so the body's feedback mechanisms still operate, unlike with injected GH. It was FDA-approved for diagnosing and treating growth hormone deficiency in children before manufacturing ceased in 2008. Reviews describe the hormonal mechanism as real, with limited controlled evidence of visible body-composition change in healthy adults.

paras: Available through compounding pharmacies and telehealth clinics, prescribed off-label as an injectable for age-related decline, body composition and recovery. Users typically report sleep and recovery changes over weeks and body changes over months.

Prescription-only in the US and banned in competitive sport. Common effects are injection-site reactions, flushing and headache. It is avoided with active cancer and in pregnancy. Compounded preparation quality and telehealth marketing claims are reported to vary.

angle.text: Sermorelin prompts your own pituitary to release more growth hormone, aiming at a leaner body, better sleep and recovery, and for some teenagers added height. It was approved in the past for diagnosing and treating GH deficiency in children. Use for cosmetic or height goals in healthy people is off-label and untested.

lead: Sermorelin (sermorelin acetate; brand names Geref and Gerel) is a synthetic peptide made of the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), thought to be the shortest fully active fragment of the natural 44-amino-acid hormone. It binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary gland and prompts the body's own growth hormone (GH) release, which then raises levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) [1][2][3].

People who seek sermorelin for appearance describe a chain of effects: more GH pulses, then a leaner body composition, better sleep and recovery, more capacity to train, and in some accounts firmer skin and fuller hair. These are the effects promoted by telehealth and anti-ageing clinics and described by adult users on bodybuilding forums such as T Nation [2][4][5][6][7]. Teenagers on looksmax.org have also discussed pairing it with other growth-hormone-raising compounds in the hope of gaining height before growth plates close [8].

The US Food and Drug Administration approved sermorelin in 1997 as a diagnostic agent for growth hormone secretion and as a treatment for children with growth hormone deficiency or growth failure. The manufacturer stopped production in 2008 for commercial reasons not related to safety, and sermorelin is no longer sold as an approved product, though US compounding pharmacies can prepare it on prescription and doctors can prescribe it off label [1][2]. Reviews of peptides in sport and medicine describe its hormonal mechanism and note that controlled data on visible body-composition or cosmetic outcomes in healthy adults are limited; it is prohibited in competitive sport [9][10][11][12].
infobox: 1997 (diagnostic use and pediatric growth hormone deficiency); production ceased 2008 [1][2]
Compounded and prescribed off label; not an approved marketed product [1][2]

paras: In physique and anti-ageing circles sermorelin is used with the aim of leaner body composition, better recovery between training sessions, deeper sleep and a younger look. A T Nation member said that on sermorelin or the related peptide GHRP-2 he stayed leaner and could be freer with his diet [7]. Another said his wife used it for skin turnover, hair growth, sleep and a subtle metabolic lift [4], and another called his months on it a kind of 'second puberty' with better-feeling joints [5]. A lifter on a transformation-challenge thread said he planned a few months on it while bulking in the hope of adding muscle [13].

Clinics that prescribe it market it for age-related decline in GH, improved skin elasticity, reduced wrinkles and better hair growth, according to Grokipedia, which also notes that sources describe limited scientific evidence for those cosmetic effects in healthy adults [2]. A narrative review of GH secretagogues in men with low testosterone describes sermorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, ibutamoren and ipamorelin as potent GH and IGF-1 stimulators that can improve body composition, while saying clinical efficacy data remain limited [10].

On looksmax.org a 17-year-old described a plan to combine sermorelin with the oral compound MK-677 for several months, hoping to reach a target height before his growth plates closed; other members in the thread replied that this would not raise height [8]. The topic belongs to a broader height-maximisation discussion in which GH and IGF-1 are central. No published trial has tested sermorelin for height in healthy adolescents.

Sermorelin was developed as a truncated synthetic analogue of GHRH and introduced mainly as a diagnostic tool for GH secretion in children with suspected deficiency. It was also used to treat children with GH deficiency or growth failure by stimulating the pituitary to release GH [1]. A published review covers its use in diagnosing and treating idiopathic GH deficiency in children [14].

Its use declined in the early 2000s as other diagnostic approaches and recombinant hormone assays became more widely available [1]. Wikipedia notes that GHRH levels fall with age and that sermorelin has been proposed as an alternative to recombinant GH replacement in older adults, but that no conclusive results show benefit in adults [1].

Natural GHRH is a 44-amino-acid peptide made by neurons in the hypothalamus. It reaches the anterior pituitary through the portal blood supply and binds the GHRH receptor, driving GH production and release mainly through the cyclic AMP pathway. It is released in pulses, and the hormone somatostatin opposes it, the two together shaping GH pulses; GHRH also promotes slow-wave sleep [3].

Sermorelin mimics the active end of that hormone. Because it works through the pituitary's own control loop, GH release stays subject to somatostatin feedback, which Wikipedia describes as making overdose difficult compared with injected recombinant GH and as producing pulsatile rather than constant GH release [1]. Wikipedia attributes to a 2006 review the further suggestions that sermorelin supports GH gene transcription and helps preserve pituitary function in ageing, and presents these as claims rather than established findings [1]. Growth hormone secretagogues divide into GHRH receptor agonists, which include sermorelin, CJC-1295 and tesamorelin, and ghrelin-receptor agonists such as GHRP-2, ipamorelin and MK-677 (ibutamoren) [15].

A review of PEGylated GRF analogues states that native GRF(1-29), the sermorelin sequence, retains bioactivity in vitro and is almost as effective as the full hormone at eliciting GH secretion in vivo, but has a short plasma half-life of about 10 to 20 minutes in humans because of kidney filtration and enzymatic breakdown at its N-terminus [16]. The review presents PEGylation as one approach to longer-lived forms [16]. The short half-life is one reason longer-acting analogues such as CJC-1295 have attracted interest in peptide circles [3].
Published human work on sermorelin consists mainly of older pediatric diagnostic and treatment studies, with limited controlled data in healthy or ageing adults.

Children: A review of sermorelin's use in diagnosing and treating idiopathic growth hormone deficiency in children summarises the studies that supported its approval [14]. A study of GH physiology in pregnancy gave sermorelin to five pregnant women at term before caesarean section to examine maternal and fetal pituitary and placental GH secretion [17].

Adults and ageing: A review of GH secretagogues in hypogonadal men says the compounds it covers, including sermorelin, are potent GH and IGF-1 stimulators that can improve body composition, but states that data on clinical efficacy remain limited [10]. A 2026 narrative review of peptides in urology and sexual medicine, which screened 725 records and included 76 studies, notes that GH secretagogues reliably raise GH while clinical evidence is limited, and describes tesamorelin as one of the more clinically established agents [11].

Registered trials: ClinicalTrials.gov lists studies of GHRH, the class to which sermorelin belongs, in elderly adults, in healthy men, in abdominal obesity, in HIV-associated lipodystrophy, in congestive heart failure and in mild cognitive impairment, several of them small or terminated early [18][19][20][21][22][23][24]. Tesamorelin, the stabilised 44-amino-acid GHRH analogue, was approved by the FDA in 2010 for HIV-associated abdominal fat accumulation [25].
No published randomized trial has tested sermorelin for cosmetic outcomes in healthy adults.

Grokipedia lists injection-site reactions as the most common adverse effect, with rarer headache and flushing, and notes that long-term safety data in adults are limited. It adds that GH therapies in general carry potential risks such as joint pain, effects on glucose handling and cancer concerns [2]. Wikipedia's article on GH therapy notes that GH can reduce insulin sensitivity, and that a 2011 FDA review found evidence on increased mortality inconclusive [26].

Reviews of peptides in sport and bodybuilding warn that clinical evidence is limited, that published studies examine controlled therapeutic regimens rather than the combined protocols used in physique culture, and that the largely unregulated supply chain can yield mislabeled or contaminated products [9][27]. They name cardiovascular strain, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia and psychiatric instability as emerging concerns for peptide use in sport [9]. A survey by European agencies of medicines seized in a 2014 international enforcement week examined falsified peptide and protein injectables [28].

In the United States sermorelin is a prescription-only peptide. Its commercial brand was discontinued in 2008, and a 2013 FDA determination found the Geref products were not withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness, so generic versions remain legally possible [1][2]. Today it is available chiefly as a compounded preparation. US compounding law distinguishes pharmacies that prepare patient-specific prescriptions under section 503A from outsourcing facilities under section 503B, both created or clarified by the 2013 Drug Quality and Security Act [29].

The FDA maintains public lists of bulk substances that may present significant safety risks when compounded. Its page lists several related peptides, including GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and ipamorelin, citing immunogenicity concerns and, for some, serious adverse events reported in patients; the page does not mention sermorelin [30]. Wikipedia notes that sermorelin can be prescribed off label without the legal restrictions that apply to recombinant GH, which has fuelled anti-ageing and performance use [1][2].

The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits GHRH and its analogues. Analytical studies have developed detection methods for sermorelin and related peptides in plasma and urine, though one 2021 validation study notes that such analogues do not appear to have been found in accredited laboratories' anti-doping samples [12].

Sermorelin was developed in the late twentieth century during research into peptide regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis. The FDA approved it in 1997; Geref production ended in 2008 [1][2]. Grokipedia adds that the new drug applications were withdrawn in 2009 and that the compound remains eligible for generic approval [2]. Since then it has been available through compounding pharmacies [2].

The wider story is one of pituitary extracts giving way to recombinant hormone. Cadaver-derived GH was discontinued in 1985 after a link to Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, and today GH is made by recombinant DNA technology [26]. Secretagogues such as sermorelin entered diagnostic practice as a way to test GH reserve, and later became a prescribing niche in anti-ageing medicine.

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: Sermorelin appears on T Nation mainly in the posts of adult men on testosterone replacement or enclomiphene programs, who describe adding it alongside clinic-supervised treatment [6][31]. Reported motives include leaner physique, sleep and joint feel, with some posters asking for experiences rather than reporting them [5][6][7]. One poster said that after six months on a bedtime regimen he concluded it was ineffective for men over 60 and added a second peptide [31].

On looksmax.org the discussion centres on teenagers and height, usually alongside MK-677 [8]. Sermorelin is generally grouped with the GH secretagogue family, which also includes ipamorelin, CJC-1295 and tesamorelin [15].

Anti-ageing and men's-health clinics offer sermorelin as a prescription peptide, often alongside testosterone or enclomiphene programs. Wikipedia describes the off-label route and compounding supply as the basis for this market [1], and reviews of peptide therapy in sports medicine describe a parallel 'gray market' of unapproved compounds operating largely outside regulatory oversight [27].

Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a stabilised version of full-length GHRH developed and produced by Theratechnologies and approved in 2010 for HIV-associated lipodystrophy; reported effects include injection-site reactions, swelling in the extremities and joint pain, and it may impair glucose tolerance [25]. CJC-1295 is another GHRH analogue, and ipamorelin and GHRP-2 act on the ghrelin receptor [3][15]. Orthopaedic and sports-medicine reviews group sermorelin with these agents among peptides whose preclinical findings are promising but where clinical trials are lacking [32][27].

lore.intro: Sermorelin is discussed on looksmax.org in teenage height plans alongside MK-677, and on T Nation by adult users describing leaner physiques, anti-ageing, sleep and joint effects [8][4][5][6].

claims.claim: Sermorelin with MK-677 can add height in a teenager with open growth plates.
Sermorelin keeps users leaner and can act as an anti-ageing treatment.
Sermorelin improves sleep and joint comfort.
Sermorelin does not work in men over 60.
Sermorelin is a gentler alternative to injecting growth hormone because the body keeps its own feedback.
Sermorelin is a legal, doctor-supervised route to higher growth hormone.
Growth hormone peptides help with body composition in people with low testosterone.

timeline.event: Cadaver-derived growth hormone is discontinued after a link to Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease; recombinant GH becomes the standard [26].
FDA approves sermorelin for pediatric growth hormone deficiency and diagnostic use [1][2].
A BioDrugs review summarises sermorelin in diagnosing and treating idiopathic GH deficiency in children [14].
Manufacturer discontinues Geref production for commercial reasons [1].
New drug applications withdrawn, per one summary [2].
FDA approves the related GHRH analogue tesamorelin for HIV-associated lipodystrophy [25].
FDA determines the Geref products were not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons [1]; the Drug Quality and Security Act reshapes US compounding law [29].
Review of GH secretagogues including sermorelin in hypogonadal men states clinical efficacy data remain limited [10].
FDA lists several GH-releasing peptides in its category 2 bulk-substance safety-risk list [30].
Reviews describe sermorelin among peptides with limited clinical evidence in sport and sexual medicine [27][9][11].
